notes: DCM Shriram Ltd (NSE: DCMSHRIRAM) — diversified Indian agribusiness/industrial conglomerate. Three main segments: (1) Chloro-Vinyl (caustic soda, PVC, cement, power), (2) Sugar (4 plants in UP, ~38,000 TCD crushing capacity + ethanol distilleries + co-gen), (3) Agri-Inputs (Shriram Bioseed, Shriram Farm Solutions). Also Fenesta windows. Indian fiscal year ends March 31; FY24 = year ending Mar 2024. All values in INR millions (1 INR crore = INR 10 million; standard reported figures in crore are multiplied by 10). Source: annual reports filed with BSE/NSE, investor presentations on dcmshriram.com. Sugar segment heavily exposed to UP cane SAP and government ethanol blending policy. FY22-23 saw record results on chemicals + sugar tailwinds; FY24 weaker on chloro-vinyl downcycle and sugar margin compression; FY25 modest recovery. Sector classified as Diversified Agribusiness for comps. No primary land acreage carried — operations are processing/manufacturing-led. Figures rounded; not from machine-readable filings.

periods.notes: FY21 (Apr20-Mar21): revenue Rs 7,690 cr. EBITDA Rs 1,320 cr. PAT Rs 753 cr. Strong year — caustic soda recovery + sugar export incentives. Net debt low post-deleveraging.
FY22: revenue Rs 9,540 cr. Record EBITDA Rs 1,900 cr on caustic + epichlorohydrin price spike. PAT Rs 1,142 cr.
FY23: revenue Rs 11,320 cr. EBITDA still strong Rs 1,850 cr on full-year sugar/ethanol momentum + late-cycle chemical pricing. PAT Rs 976 cr. Capex ramp pushing net debt up.
FY24: revenue Rs 11,070 cr (-2% YoY). EBITDA Rs 950 cr (-49% YoY) on caustic soda price collapse + sugar margin compression. PAT Rs 376 cr. Capex into Bharuch chemicals expansion lifting net debt.

FY25: revenue Rs 11,900 cr (+7% YoY). EBITDA Rs 760 cr (-20% YoY) — chloro-vinyl still soft, sugar/ethanol mixed on diversion caps. PAT Rs 227 cr. Bharuch project commissioning lifting D&A; FY26 expected recovery as new capacity ramps.
